searchText: With just a few validators in a single node in interop and without transactions I have trouble in Capella below 5 seconds per block Payment channels or centrally sequenced L2s are a more appropriate solution than trying to settle every second. Legacy financial systems settle daily, and only M-F, yet you can still use them to buy coffee. L2 could not post tx faster than mainnet block time, so as of now L2 solves only capacity issue, but not speed issue Visa/Master network does take days to settle tx, however, users expect all pending tx will settle except a tiny portion of it get reversed. And it’s very fast to post a tx. ETH ecosystem needs a way to quickly post tx into a block, but can let tx take many blocks(minutes) to finality and expect re-org is rare - this is why short block time changes the game L2 could not post tx faster than mainnet <dannyryan> L2s can make crypto economic commitments for fast confs but would not have the security of L1 until posted on there <dannyryan> But that can definitely improve UX for paying for coffee/etc Yea, those are the fallout of the architectural decisions that allow thousands of nodes and half a million validators. Some BFTs can have sub-second latency but break down at the low hundreds of validators.
